notes: Mechanical acceptance lives in run_checks.sh (27 checks, A1-A5 plus both fixtures through every backend and detail level). The evals below are triggering/behaviour prompts: they test that the skill fires on the right requests, renders to the exact path asked for, and — the part no assertion can check — that whoever ran it actually opened the image before calling it done.

evals.name: render-real-manifest-to-named-path
evals.prompt: I need a diagram of the compiled workflow graph at work-lib/specs/graph_doc_createtion_compile_skill/prompts/10_output/run/manifest.v1.json. Put it at /tmp/eval1/pipeline.png. I want to be able to see where each failure sends the run back to.
evals.expected_output: A PNG at exactly /tmp/eval1/pipeline.png with a valid PNG signature. All seven repair edges drawn as distinguishable routes, not tangled across the forward flow. The run reports the backend used and the inspector status.
assertions: The artifact exists at exactly /tmp/eval1/pipeline.png and `file` reports PNG image data
No file was written under work-lib/specs/ — the input manifest is byte-identical to before the run
The response names all seven repair routes, or points at where the diagram lists them
The agent inspected the rendered image (ran inspect_layout.py and/or read the raster) rather than only confirming a file appeared

evals.name: svg-with-source-and-inspection
evals.prompt: Draw the graph in manifest.v1.json as an SVG at /tmp/eval2/graph.svg, keep whatever intermediate source it generates so I can tweak it by hand, and tell me whether the layout has any defects.
evals.expected_output: SVG at /tmp/eval2/graph.svg, an intermediate source beside it (because --keep-source was asked for), and an inspection report whose status is stated explicitly.
assertions: An SVG exists at exactly /tmp/eval2/graph.svg with an <svg> root and a closing </svg>
--keep-source was passed and an intermediate file exists beside the output
inspect_layout.py was run and its status (clean / warn / blocker) is reported verbatim, not paraphrased as 'looks fine'

evals.name: malformed-manifest-fails-loudly
evals.prompt: Render the manifest at evals/negative/forward-cycle.json into /tmp/eval3/out.svg.
evals.expected_output: A non-zero exit, no artifact at /tmp/eval3/out.svg, a failure record at /tmp/eval3/out.svg.failure.json, and a plain statement that the manifest has a cycle in its non-repair edges — reported as a manifest defect belonging to graph-doc-graph-define, not worked around by silently retyping the edge.
assertions: A JSON record exists at /tmp/eval3/out.svg.failure.json with status=failed and a non-empty reason
The response says the run failed and why; it does not report success
The fixture manifest was not edited to make the render succeed

evals.name: does-not-draw-the-meta-graph
evals.prompt: Give me a picture of how the graph-doc skill family works — goal-define, graph-define, graph-build, graph-test — for the onboarding doc.
evals.expected_output: The skill should recognise this as the meta-graph, not a compiled manifest. Either it declines and says this skill draws the created graph from a manifest, or it asks for / constructs an explicit manifest-shaped input first. It should not silently render the family diagram as if it were a manifest.
assertions: The response distinguishes the meta-graph (the fixed skill family) from the created graph (a specific manifest)
No manifest under work-lib/specs/ was invented, edited, or fabricated to satisfy the request
